The singer disclosed this in a post on his X account on Friday, saying his foundation would expand its usual birthday donations to motherless babies’ homes to include financial support for aspiring entrepreneurs. Davido said the initiative was informed by the economic difficulties facing many Nigerians and the need to help people turn their business ideas into reality. “This year for my birthday, my foundation will not only be sending money to the motherless babies’ homes as usual … we also want to help Nigerians with start-up funds for their business ideas as we know how difficult the situation in the country has been. We start Monday,” he wrote. The initiative is expected to commence on Monday, November 23, two days after the singer’s birthday on November 21. However, Davido did not disclose the amount earmarked for the programme, the number of beneficiaries or the criteria for selecting applicants. He also did not provide details on how interested Nigerians could submit their business proposals. The announcement marks an expansion of the singer’s annual birthday charity activities, which have traditionally included donations to motherless babies’ homes and orphanages. In November 2021, Davido raised ₦200 million from friends and associates and added ₦50 million of his own money, bringing the donation to ₦250 million for orphanages across Nigeria. The singer later established the David Adeleke Foundation to give structure to his philanthropic activities. His latest announcement has introduced business support as another focus of his birthday giving, with further details of the funding initiative expected as the programme begins.
